clue.text: Authorisation of combat leading to diatribe

clue.text: Complaint from women on dating app

explanation.definitionFit: A whinge is a peevish moan, the British colloquial word for a grumbling grievance.

clue.text: Decline is rubbish

explanation.walkthrough: The two meanings are pronounced differently: re-FUSE the verb and REF-use the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To refuse is to turn down an offer, and refuse is household waste collected by bin men.

clue.text: Time on the radio tackling Duke is making spectacular show

taken as written

clue.text: Small person tense with desire

explanation.walkthrough: Titch is British slang for a very short person.
explanation.definitionFit: Titch is an informal British nickname for someone tiny, often a child.

clue.text: Creature with many feet and abnormal growth on display, at first

parts.note: opening letter
opening letter

clue.text: Letter to Sakellaropoulou's supporting commoner's figure of speech

explanation.walkthrough: Katerina Sakellaropoulou was President of Greece, so her letter is a Greek one; in a down clue the supporting piece goes underneath.

clue.text: Plumber regularly discarded oil

parts.note: dropping the first, fourth and seventh letters keeps the rest

clue.text: Tentatively schedule antibiotic I left out (in different places)

taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: To pencil in an appointment is to book it provisionally, as pencil marks can be rubbed out.

clue.text: Avoid going across island to get prize?

parts.note: to dodge is to evade

explanation.surface: Someone skirts round an island hoping to claim an award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prize' looks like an award, but it is the British spelling variant of prise, to force out with a lever; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: To dislodge something is to force it out of position, exactly what prising does with a lever.

clue.text: Conclude popular official has been recalled

clue.text: Instruments found in dead body turned over by doctor

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sawbones' is old slang for a surgeon, and Bones is the doctor in Star Trek; mort is French for a dead person.
explanation.definitionFit: Trombones are brass instruments played by moving a slide to change pitch.

clue.text: Terrible rage about insignificant smoking aid?

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
slight means small or unimportant

explanation.surface: A furious outburst over a trivial thing to do with smoking.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits a gas lighter lights cigarettes but is not strictly made for smoking.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas lighter is a butane lighter, the device a smoker uses to light up.

clue.text: Singer sampled by Eminem achieved nothing

parts.note: past tense of do, to accomplish
O is the zero shape for nothing

explanation.definitionFit: Dido's track Thank You was used as the hook of Eminem's 2000 hit Stan.

clue.text: Give cash to adopt hairstyle: single dollar bill?

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark shows a dollar bill is one example.

clue.text: Careful! Pakistan gin is abysmal

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'statesman' as state's man: a man from a US state, here Indiana.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indianian is a resident of Indiana, so literally a man of an American state.

clue.text: Scientific apparatus made from grates under ring

indicators.note: under places one part beneath the other in this down entry

parts.note: to ring someone is to give them a bell

explanation.definitionFit: Bell jars are glass domes used in laboratories to hold a vacuum or protect specimens.

clue.text: Again provide super cast with work, steadily

parts.note: the eleven letters to rearrange

clue.text: Bless a number at home time

someone at home is in

clue.text: Praise of Monet, perhaps, unbounded

parts.note: Claude Monet, the Impressionist, is one example of a Claude

taken as written

clue.text: Helping others to hide gold block, perhaps
